answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a time-bound stake that is forfeited on duplicate behavior. Registering a second identity forces an attacker to escrow fresh collateral again, and accounts that mirror bids or message timing get their deposit slashed. This makes each fake identity cost the full stake, so flooding a market with puppets becomes uneconomical. Agents needing bulk leverage, like trading desks in timber futures, saffron importers, or onyx miners, can act through one bonded account instead of spawning copies.
